title: Agent Evaluation Reliability: More Tasks Won't (Always) Fix An Agent Leaderboard
abstract: arXiv:2610.00651v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent evaluations are increasingly used to compare LLMs and inform deployment decisions, yet ranks can reflect not only the model but also the effects of the evaluation conditions such as the scaffolds or tasks. This makes reliability claim-dependent: an evaluation that reliably ranks deployed systems may not reliably rank underlying models. We ask which conclusions current agent evaluations reliably support and what additional evaluation would improve them. We develop a Bayesian variance-decomposition framework for sparse, imbalanced agent leaderboards and apply it to 22 benchmarks from the Holistic Agent Leaderboard and Harbor Index. translated_title: 智能体评估的可靠性：更多任务并不（总是）能修复智能体排行榜
translated_abstract: 智能体评估越来越多地被用于比较大型语言模型（LLM）并为部署决策提供依据，然而排名不仅可能反映模型本身，还可能反映评估条件（如智能体支架或任务）的影响。这使得可靠性依赖于具体的评估声明：一项能够可靠地排名已部署系统的评估，可能无法可靠地排名底层模型。我们探讨当前的智能体评估能够可靠支持哪些结论，以及什么样的额外评估可以改进这些结论。我们为稀疏且不平衡的智能体排行榜开发了一个贝叶斯方差分解框架，并将其应用于来自 Holistic Agent Leaderboard 和 Harbor Index 的22个基准测试。该框架将信号（与目标评估声明相关的性能差异）与噪声（仍可能改变排名的无关变化）分离开来。我们发现：（1）可靠性取决于测量目标。固定的模型-支架系统能够被可靠地排名（0.935-0.994），而底层模型的可靠性……
tldr: 该论文提出一个贝叶斯方差分解框架来评估稀疏且不平衡的智能体排行榜，发现评估可靠性取决于测量目标——固定模型-支架系统可被可靠排名，但底层模型排名受噪声干扰，因此单纯增加任务数量并不总能修复智能体排行榜的可靠性问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a Bayesian variance-decomposition framework for sparse, imbalanced agent leaderboards, showing that reliability is claim-dependent—fixed model-scaffold systems can be ranked reliably while underlying-model rankings are affected by noise—so simply adding more tasks won't always fix an agent leaderboard.
